subject: Psychology
central_question: How is information encoded, retained and retrieved through different memory systems, why does forgetting occur and how can memory improve?
in_scope_units: Atkinson and Shiffrin’s information-processing stage model.
Attention, maintenance rehearsal, chunking and elaborative rehearsal.
Declarative, procedural, episodic and semantic memory.
Recall, recognition, sentence verification and priming.
Forgetting curve and trace decay, interference and retrieval failure.
Proactive and retroactive interference and repressed memories.
Mnemonics, organisation, deep processing, retrieval cues and PQRST.
banned_topics: Detailed conditioning procedures, which belong to Learning.
Clinical diagnosis and treatment of amnesia beyond the chapter’s examples.

known_pitfalls.correction: The chapter presents several processes, systems and long-term memory types.

known_pitfalls.claim: Rote repetition always gives the best retention.
known_pitfalls.correction: Semantic and elaborative processing creates stronger associations.

known_pitfalls.claim: Forgetting always means a trace disappeared.
known_pitfalls.correction: Interference or missing retrieval cues may make stored information inaccessible.

known_pitfalls.claim: Recognition and recall are the same.
known_pitfalls.correction: Recall generates information; recognition identifies previously encountered items.

recommended_example_progression: NCERT Review Question 1 on encoding, storage and retrieval.
NCERT Review Question 4 on long-term memory types.
NCERT Review Question 7 on memory improvement.
ncert_end_of_chapter_exercises_reference: The chapter ends with Review Questions 1–7 and one Project Idea.
